answer: A reputation trellis resists sybils by making trust expensive to fake: every agent must lock a refundable stake and earn endorsements only from peers with a history of verified work, so a fresh identity starts with no voting or reward power. A signed audit trail acts as a quill that records each claim and endorsement, and random spot-checks shine a lantern on clusters of new accounts that endorse one another, slashing their stake when collusion is found. Mass fake identities then cost real money and time, while honest agents keep their standing.
